source.title: Memorization in image classification: test set behavior and scaling laws

record.file_problem: None; the full paper text, including appendices, is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study measures test-set label fit during training, providing a different test of epoch-wise behavior. It does not measure the double-descent shape across model sizes or training-set sizes.
record.gate_note: The width and dataset-size experiments report training accuracy and memorization time, not test error, so they do not provide rows for V1 or V3. For V2, the study reports test-set label-fit trajectories in Figure 1 and states that test accuracy remains near chance in the random-label condition. No results test the remaining versions.
record.test_reason: The study does not test double descent. It is about memorization on random labels and random pixels. Its only test-time curves (Figure 1) are plotted without any description of a fall-rise-fall shape. The width × dataset-size experiments report training accuracy and time-to-interpolate, not test error. Belkin et al. is cited only as background.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. Networks memorizing arbitrary labels agree on training examples but make initialization-dependent, confident, disagreeing predictions on test inputs. The presentations per example needed to memorize fall with dataset size, even for random pixels, and this depends on the batch-size/learning-rate policy.
record.recipe_differences: The study examines predictive behavior and memorization efficiency in CIFAR-10 CNNs, rather than measuring test-risk double descent across model size, epochs, or sample size.
record.method_sensitivity: Memorization efficiency varies with the joint batch-size/learning-rate policy, especially for random-pixel inputs; this is reported for training-time outcomes, not test-error double descent.

fits_no_version.finding: The width needed to interpolate the training set grows with dataset size. The memorization frontier is roughly linear in log-width vs log-dataset-size, with slopes of about 0.2–0.93 depending on labels, pixels and batch policy.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The location of the interpolation threshold (capacity needed to fit n samples) scales as a power of n and depends on label/input structure and optimization policy.

fits_no_version.finding: Epochs to reach 95% training accuracy fall with dataset size as roughly a + b/n, even for random labels and random pixels.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Time-to-interpolate per example decreases with dataset size even without shared structure.

record.peer_reviewed: 40th Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS 2026), Workshop: Neural Network Artifacts as a New Data Modality
record.problems: The predictive-dynamics experiment uses one architecture and width, and the test-set label-fit curves are presented in plots without numerical values. The random-pixel trajectories are described as irregular; each memorization-frontier configuration has a single run.

untested.parts: No test-error sweep over width; only training accuracy across widths (Figure 2).
The true-label test-loss trajectory is plotted but not described; no claim about its shape.
Dataset size is varied, but only training accuracy and epochs-to-memorize are reported, not test error.
Not addressed; random labels are full noise, not a noise sweep.

missing.what: Test accuracy was evaluated after every epoch in all 240 memorization-frontier runs (width × fraction) but is not reported. It would be the data needed for V1/V3 test-error sweeps.
Numerical or descriptive test cross-entropy trajectory over epochs for the true-label ensemble.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's 'tests/T2' and V2 'challenges' label are rejected. The random-label and random-pixel test curves cannot bear on epoch-wise double descent because there is no generalizable signal. The study is relevant to interpolation-threshold location only as a related construct, measured via training accuracy.

versions.untested_parts: No test-error sweep over model size is reported.
Tests a 4×-width CNN ensemble on CIFAR-10 conditions, not a broad sweep of models or training regimes.
Dataset size is varied, but the reported outcomes are training accuracy and training time, not test error near an interpolation threshold.
No general double-descent test across model classes.
No single effective-complexity measure is tested across size, epochs, or samples.
No test of noise/regularization dependence, multiple peaks, or optimally tuned regularization.
No alternative parameter-count measure or reanalysis of a second-descent curve.
